name: Low-dose onabotulinumtoxinA in noncatheterizing MS
question: Does intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U reduce urinary incontinence versus placebo in noncatheterizing adults with multiple sclerosis and neurogenic detrusor overactivity?

design.population: Adults with stable multiple sclerosis, neurogenic detrusor overactivity and urinary incontinence despite anticholinergic treatment who were not catheterizing at baseline.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority randomized trial
design.locator: Full text, Methods: Study design and Patients; Results: Patients

verdictNote: Week 6 incontinence reduction met the primary superiority hypothesis.
takeaway: In noncatheterizing adults with multiple sclerosis and neurogenic detrusor overactivity, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 100 U reduced daily urinary incontinence episodes more than placebo at week 6; urinary infection and initiation of intermittent catheterization were more frequent.

reports.label: Primary randomized report
reports.citation: Tullman M, Chartier-Kastler E, Kohan A, et al. "Low-dose onabotulinumtoxinA improves urinary symptoms in noncatheterizing patients with MS." *Neurology.* 2018;91(7):e657-e665. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000005991
reports.followUp: 12-week placebo-controlled period; follow-up to 52 weeks, with optional open-label retreatment

results.measure: Week 6 mean change from baseline; between-arm mean difference in episodes/day
results.note: Difference calculated from the rounded arm changes in the abstract.

results.endpoint: Incontinence Quality of Life total score
results.measure: Week 6 mean change from baseline in I-QOL points
results.note: The reported minimally important difference was +11 points.

results.measure: Median weeks from first treatment to retreatment request
results.note: Retreatment, when given, was open-label onabotulinumtoxinA.

harms.label: Protocol-defined urinary tract infection, first 12 weeks
harms.note: Culture plus leukocyturia defined UTI regardless of symptoms.

harms.label: Symptomatic urinary tract infection, first 12 weeks
Hospitalization for urinary tract infection, treatment cycle 1
harms.note: Two of the three hospitalizations occurred in the first 12 weeks; a placebo count was not reported.

harms.label: Initiation of clean intermittent catheterization for retention, treatment cycle 1
harms.locator: Full text, Results: Safety; Abstract: Results
harms.note: At any time during treatment cycle 1; median catheterization duration was 64.0 versus 2.0 days.

delivery.label: Injection technique
delivery.value: Cystoscopic delivery as 30 one-mL detrusor injections, evenly distributed while avoiding the trigone; local anesthesia was usual.

delivery.label: Open-label second treatment
delivery.locator: Full text, Methods: Study design; Results: Efficacy
delivery.note: After at least 12 weeks, patient request, at least 2 episodes over 3 days, and postvoid residual <200 mL.
